toegepas.rede_vinder: The block is about inventors, and 'gemaak' (made) is vaguer than 'uitgevind', which the next sentences use.
toegepas.fout: 'gemaak' is vague in a block about who invented something
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'uitgevind' is the exact verb for an inventor, matches the next sentence, and leaves the protected sentence untouched.

toegepas.rede_vinder: Televisie is one word, so saying it 'sounds like' one word is illogical; the point is that it looks like a single word but has two parts.
toegepas.fout: 'klink na een woord' is illogical, since televisie is one word that only appears to be a single unit
toegepas.rede_keurder: 'lyk soos een woord' says clearly that it appears to be one word but has two parts, with no change to what is claimed.

laat_vaar.rede_vinder: In Afrikaans the prepositional phrase normally comes before the predicate adjective: 'nie vir kinders geskik nie'.
laat_vaar.rede_keurder: 'nie geskik vir kinders nie' is already natural Afrikaans, so moving the phrase is a lateral change.

na_skrywer.voor: uit te stuur, en nie na gekose mense nie
na_skrywer.na: uit te stuur en nie na gekose mense nie
na_skrywer.rede_vinder: AWS: no comma before 'en' between parts of one sentence; the clause has no own subject and verb, and the kleurtelevisie entry already writes the same pattern without one.
na_skrywer.fout: under the house AWS rule a comma before 'en' joining parts of one sentence is not allowed, though it can be defended as a contrast comma
na_skrywer.rede_keurder: This is a glossary definition that may be shared, and a defensible contrast comma is not a plain error, so the writer has to change it in every lesson at once.
na_skrywer.waarom: the reviewer sent it to the writer

laat_vaar_vorige.voor: sien maar nie terwyl dit gebeur nie
laat_vaar_vorige.na: sien, maar nie terwyl dit gebeur nie
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_vinder: A comma before the contrasting 'maar nie ...' element makes the contrast easier for a Grade 4 reader to follow; AWS permits it here.
laat_vaar_vorige.rede_keurder: Here 'maar nie terwyl dit gebeur nie' is a shortened contrast inside one sentence, not a second sentence with its own subject and verb, so the house AWS rule does not call for a comma; the short original already reads clearly and the comma would be a lateral change.
